children: Data-center power and cooling supplier Vertiv

modeled up to 30% more cumulative AI token output during a project's first year using NVIDIA DSX, while its shares traded at $193.80, down 8.65%, at approximately 11:46 a.m. ET Thursday. The pitch is simple: get the infrastructure running sooner, and customers have more time to put expensive computing equipment to work.

Vertiv's scenario cuts design and validation from 30 days to three, then halves infrastructure deployment from 90 days to 45. That creates 317 productive days rather than 245 at the same installed capacity. These are modeled gains, with actual results dependent on execution. Polar Data Centers is applying the factory-built approach to the first 41-megawatt phase of its Herya campus in Norway, giving investors a project to watch.

The valuation snapshot puts the shares 7.15% above the $180.86 GF Value estimate, suggesting the selloff has not erased the valuation premium. Vertiv's second-quarter results showed an adjusted operating margin of 22.6%, up 410 basis points year over year. That supports the operating story. The next test is whether faster deployment translates into reliable capacity for customers and profitable growth for Vertiv.

title: Vertiv Stocks Fall 8.65% Despite Faster AI-Factory Deployment Model
